notes.title: Another Quick Update
notes.notes:
I wanted to give an update on my progress. I’m not really happy with how things turned out last month. 

I spent the last month working on a feature that I thought would be simple to add: Kitchen windows. It turned out to be much more complex than I had anticipated, and I had to rewrite a lot of existing code in order to get the kitchen windows to work. 

To make matters worse, when I eventually did get them to work on a technical level, I found out that they were not working on a gameplay level. Using kitchen windows almost never actually made a restaurant more efficient. Which means that they are essentially useless. 

I’ve experimented with multiple ways to solve this issue, but none of the experiments really went anywhere. I’m sure that there is a solution that I’m missing, but I already spend much more time on kitchen windows than I intended to. That’s why I decided to set the kitchen window idea aside for now, and focus on more important issues. Hopefully I can return to the idea in the future. 

I pushed the latest build with kitchen windows to the experimental branch, so you can still play around with them. Please let me know if you have any suggestions on how to improve them. 

The kitchen window idea not working out was a huge disappointment. But it did have some good side effects. It allowed me to rewrite a lot of important code, and reflect on my game design process. I hope that I can prevent this kind of thing from happening in the future by better prioritizing what I work on.  

I will be taking a little summer break, and the game still needs some work to be stable enough for the main branch. The next update will be on the 12th of august. After this update, I will go back to regular updates. I’m really looking forward to adding exciting new features, and making TasteMaker a better game.

notes.title: Quick Update
notes.notes:
In this short blog I want to explain why the update is taking so long. 

I wanted to add kitchen serving windows to the game. This seemed like something that would be relatively easy to implement. However, it turned out to be much more complex than I anticipated. I ended up having to rewrite a lot of existing code, and this made the game very unstable. 

The kitchen window feature is now finished. Rewriting a lot of existing code also gave me the opportunity to fix some other issues. But the game is currently not very well tested and not as stable as I would like it to be. That’s why I decided to release this update on the experimental branch first. 

I’m still trying to release updates as frequently as possible. But sometimes unexpected issues show up. I hope that future updates will go a bit smoother.

notes.title: Update announcement
notes.notes:
A while back I posted a quick update blog where I announced a big update. In this blog I want to reveal a bit more about this exciting new update. 

We finally decided on a release date. The new update will be released on the 3rd of march.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37954720/3ffb3ad59aeaac1b74a59ab406689871c33b7d97.png

Content overview  

We will reveal all the details of the added content in the devblog that will be released on the 3th of march. But here is a rough overview of all the content you can expect. I think that this update will bring TasteMaker a lot closer to the vision that I originally had for the game.  

Casino games

6 more casino games will be added to the game, all fully animated. This should enable you to create complete casinos. 

Lounge

We added 4 furniture items that should enable you to build a lounge area to the game. 

Cocktails

We added 3 cocktails to the game, along with 2 new ingredients and 2 new kitchen items to make the cocktails. 

Staff

Currently, You can only hire 1 staff type. In the new update, you can hire a waiter, chef, dealer and cat. 

More

The update also includes a bunch quality of life and miscellaneous features. 

Building options

We also added some more options to build and customize your restaurant. You can currently only build 2 floors. In the new update this will be expanded, we are currently experimenting with how many floors would be optimal. 

Additionally, new items, like pillars, dividers, decoration items and floor textures will be added.  

Music and sound effects

The game never contained a lot of music or sound effects. This update will improve this by adding background music and by giving you the ability to build your own band. The sound effects in the game are also improved. 

Scenario

We are making a new scenario that will be the biggest scenario in the game. This scenario will also be part of the update.

Gameplay

Besides adding new content, I also tried to make the game more fun. I did this by rebalancing the game, and changing how things work behind the scenes. Whether I succeed is subjective, but I definitely think that this update is a step in the right direction. 

Updated trailer

The old trailer was starting to get a bit dated so we made a new trailer. This trailer also contrains some of the content.

notes.title: Quick update
notes.notes:
Quick update

I’ve been a bit quiet for the past weeks, so I thought that it would be a good idea to write a little blog to explain what I’ve been up to.


Next update

I’ve been working on adding outdoor restaurants and balconies. This turned out to be a bit more tricky than i anticipated because a lot of game mechanics/code relies on there being a clear distinction between grid tiles that are inside the restaurant and tiles that are outside the restaurant. When I add the ability to make outdoor restaurants, this distinction won’t be so clear anymore. This caused a lot of issues that had to be addressed. I will release the update to the building system on the 30th of april. 


Update cycle

Previously, I’ve released updates on a bi-weely cycle. This didn’t really work for me because some things take a bit longer to implement. The need to have a playable build every 2 weeks prevented me from making the big changes that are needed to make TasteMaker the game that I want it to be. That's why I’ve decided to release bigger, less frequent updates. These updates won’t be released on a fixed schedule. As mentioned, the next update will be on the 30th of april.


Experimental branch

I’m also planning to release updates more frequently on the experimental branch. These updates can be very unstable but if you want to preview the latest changes, you will be able to view them on there. Hopefully doing it this way can also help to make the main branch more stable.  

The devblogs will only be made for updates to the stable branch. But I might release some patch notes for the experimental branch in the discord and steam discussion group. 

The next experimental update will be released this wednesday (21st of april)


Team expansion

I’ve been talking to 2 freelance artists who will hopefully be able to start working on the game this week. This can not only increase the development speed, but also the quality of the art.

notes.title: Quick update
notes.notes:
The early access release

The release of TasteMaker exceeded all my expectations. It is amazing to hear that people enjoy the game. I also want to thank everybody for all the great feedback and suggestions. 

My apologies if I haven’t been able to reply to your feedback, I tried to reply to as many messages as I could but failed to keep up. I also made the stupid mistake of focussing most of my attention on the discord server and forgetting to check the steam forums and reddit. I will make sure that I will check the steam forums more often from now on. 

You can view the trello board with most of the feedback here


Update cycle

I plan to release updates on a predictable schedule. Hopefully this will make it easier to follow the development of the game. My current plan is to release bi-weekly updates on a Thursday. I will write a blog for every update and post it on Steam and the TasteMaker website. 


Roadmap

While the early access release has been a big milestone, it’s certainly not the end of the journey. I will keep working on TasteMaker for a long time to come. As a way to share my ideas, I’ve created a roadmap for the game. I would love to hear your feedback on it. Please keep in mind that this roadmap is not intended as a rigid planning. 

You can view the roadmap here
